divisor_proof: At the irreducible divisor A=1+4*a^2, the residue field is Q(i).  A constant j is a square in Q(i) iff j is a rational square or minus a rational square.  If the divisor is inert, every norm has even A-valuation, while A has valuation one.
endpoint_necessity: At q=0 the pulled-back norm is U^2-j*(q*V)^2=h and ord_q(h)=-8.  Its leading residue has square class 1/A, so 1/A, equivalently A, must be a norm from Q(a,Z)(sqrt(j)).
exact_constant_twists: For nonsquare j, A is a norm iff j=-1 modulo Q^x2; explicitly A=Norm_Q(i)(1+2*a*i).  Square j is the split case.
